items.title: Contextual expression of learning motivation in out-of-school learning environment
items.abstract: This study examines how visit purpose and visit configuration (family versus school groups) are associated with engagement patterns in an out-of-school science learnıng environment, specifically the Izmir Natural Wildlife Park. Drawing on Falk and Dierking’s Contextual Model of Learning, learning motivation is conceptualized not as a latent psychological trait but as a contextually expressed process observable through engagement behaviors. A qualitative case study design was employed with 119 middle school students aged 11–14. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and systematic observations, focusing on dwell time, label reading, interaction patterns, and reported learning outcomes. Findings indicate that visit purpose differed substantially between groups: family visitors predominantly reported entertainment-oriented goals, whereas school-group visitors emphasized learning-oriented purposes. These orientations corresponded to distinct engagement patterns. School groups demonstrated longer exhibit dwell times, higher rates of label reading, and more frequent articulation of specific content knowledge. In contrast, family groups engaged more socially within their own units but interacted less with interpretive materials. Despite these differences, children in both groups perceived school-led visits as more effective for learning. Interpreted within the contextual model framework, the findings suggest that visit purpose (personal context) and group structure (sociocultural context) shape how engagement becomes behaviorally visible within the same physical environment. Rather than indicating differences in intrinsic motivation, the results highlight how motivational activation is mediated by social configuration and institutional framing. The study contributes to the literature on science education in out-of-school learning environments by comparatively examining family and school visits within a wildlife park context and by operationalizing learning motivation through observable engagement indicators. Implications for exhibit design, teacher preparation, and out-of-school science learning environments policy are discussed.

items.title: Control OSWorld: An AI Control Environment for GUI Computer Use Agents
items.abstract: AI agents that operate a computer through its graphical user interface (GUI) are being widely deployed. AI control studies how to prevent an AI system from causing harm even if it is misaligned and actively trying to do so. Most control research to date has focused on coding agents, leaving computer use largely unexplored. We introduce Control OSWorld, a control evaluation that pairs 318 tasks from OSWorld with 81 harmful side tasks (e.g., exfiltrating a private file) that an agent must complete without being caught. We use Control OSWorld to create and study control monitors that detect malicious agents interacting with a GUI. We find that a weaker monitor can reliably distinguish honest from malicious trajectories produced by a more capable agent when it sees the full trajectory (97% recall at 3% false positive rate). However, when the monitor has to score each step before it is executed, recall drops at low false positive rates because each action is judged with less context. Monitor performance also depends on what the monitor can see: access to the agent's visible text is critical, while screenshots provide little additional value.

items.title: ConvoDrift: A Multi-Turn Conversational Dataset for Modeling Stylistic Tone Evolution
items.abstract: The evolution of linguistic style in conversations is an underexplored issue in NLP. Most style-control datasets focus on sentences or assume a static style throughout, missing the dynamic shifts that occur as user preferences change during interactions. We introduce ConvoDrift, a dataset designed to model progressive stylistic conversational tone drift under fixed semantic intent. It is built on 15,727 shared multi-turn conversational structures for adaptation and persona-conditioned alignment methods. It consists of six prompt-response pairs per conversation, each with the annotation of style drift and style direction labels. These pairs cover a range of communication genres. We further derive a complementary pairwise dataset by pairing semantically equivalent but stylistically distinct responses and annotating persona-conditioned preferences using five distinct style communication personas, enabling the controlled study of personalisation and pluralistic alignment in language tone. In addition to dataset construction, we conduct a comprehensive evaluation involving human validation, LLM-as-judge assessment, and automatic lexical and semantic evaluations. Across seven Likert criteria annotated by three human annotators, the average Krippendorff's alpha is 0.88, and our lexical and semantic analyses show that drift events induce lexical changes while preserving semantic similarity.

items.title: CoR-Hate: counterfactual retrieval and fairness-regularized hate-speech detection
items.abstract: Abstract The growing presence of hate speech on social media, targeting groups based on race, religion, gender, and sexual orientation, raises critical concerns regarding fairness and reliability in automated moderation systems. This study introduces CoR-Hate, a fairness-regularized framework that integrates Sentence-Transformer-based semantic retrieval with pretrained transformer models to mitigate algorithmic bias while maintaining strong classification performance. Unlike prior approaches that construct synthetic counterfactuals through identity-term substitutions, manually defined templates, or large-language-model generation, CoR-Hate retrieves corpus-grounded counterfactual proxies from naturally occurring samples using FAISS-based similarity search. A consistency-driven regularization objective is then applied to improve prediction stability across identity-sensitive variations and reduce reliance on identity-specific cues. Comprehensive bias analysis at both entity and pairwise levels is conducted to evaluate fairness robustness across demographic attributes. Experiments on the HateXplain dataset using two Sentence-Transformer variants, all-mpnet-base-v2 and all-MiniLM-L6-v2 , demonstrate consistent improvements over baseline models. Notably, the CoR-Hate BERT model with MPNet embeddings achieves the strongest overall fairness-performance trade-off, attaining an F1-score of 0.79 and an accuracy of 0.80 while reducing the flip rate to 0.10, the lowest among all evaluated models. Furthermore, Grad-CAM-based interpretability provides transparent insights into model behaviour by visualizing token-level importance across identity substitutions. The results indicate reduced sensitivity to identity-specific terms for few evaluated substitutions, although residual bias remains for certain terms and model architectures. Importantly, a lower flip rate reflects prediction consistency only for the predefined identity substitutions and should not be interpreted as evidence that all forms of algorithmic bias have been eliminated. Overall, CoR-Hate provides a unified, corpus-grounded, and explainable framework for mitigating identity-related bias in hate speech detection.

items.title: CORNAV: Construction-Aware Reasoning for Robot Navigation on Active Worksites
items.abstract: The construction industry faces persistent labor shortages, low productivity that costs the global economy over $1.6 trillion annually, and one of the highest injury rates among major industries. These factors motivate the use of autonomous robots to improve efficiency and worker safety. Existing language-grounded navigation systems, however, rely on semantic scene understanding alone and lack access to construction-specific context such as architectural plans, evolving work schedules, and safety constraints. As a result, they localize permanent building features unreliably and cannot safely navigate active jobsites. We present CORNAV, a blueprint-grounded, schedule-aware navigation framework that operates from 2D CAD drawings and project schedules without requiring a Building Information Model. CORNAV aligns architectural blueprints against hierarchical open-vocabulary 3D scene graphs to ground object queries, converts project schedules into time-varying navigation constraints, and validates requests through an LLM-based safety module that escalates hazardous zones before planning. An A* planner then enforces mandatory exclusion zones while preferentially avoiding higher-risk areas. Across an indoor office and a real construction site, blueprint grounding raises task success from 13.0% to 72.2% over semantic retrieval alone, schedule awareness eliminates all hard-zone violations, and the safety module correctly rejects hazardous requests arising from mislabeled project schedules.

items.title: Could AI chatbots mislead orthodontic patients? An assessment from the perspectives of accuracy, risk, and ethics
items.abstract: The aim of this study is to comparatively evaluate the performance of three different Large Language Models (ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot), commonly used in orthodontic patient counseling, in terms of clinical accuracy, potential clinical risk, and ethical suitability. This prospective, cross-sectional, and scenario-based study utilized a total of 100 questions collected from orthodontic patients, categorized into five main groups (general knowledge, treatment process, emergencies, pediatric and adult orthodontics, special cases). The questions were administered to three different Large Language Models using a “zero-shot” approach between February and March 2026. The responses were evaluated by three experienced orthodontists using a 5-point Likert scale in a blinded evaluation process for accuracy, potential clinical risk, and ethical appropriateness. Data were analyzed using Repeated Measures ANOVA, and inter-observer agreement was calculated using the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) ( p ≤ 0.05). When all categories and the total dataset were evaluated, no statistically significant differences were found between the three models in terms of accuracy ( p = 0.927), potential clinical risk ( p = 0.325), and ethical appropriateness ( p = 0.060). Accuracy scores were high in all models (≈ 4.2/5), while potential clinical risk scores were concentrated in the low range (≈ 1.05–1.70). Ethical appropriateness scores were generally high (≈ 4.3–4.5). Inter-observer agreement was generally moderate-good, higher in the emergency and special circumstances categories, and lower in the pediatric and adult orthodontics categories. ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot produce similar and highly accurate responses in orthodontic patient consultation. However, the fact that potential clinical risks have not been completely eliminated and the variability in ethical guidelines highlight the need for these systems to be used as a support tool under physician supervision, rather than as independent clinical decision-making tools. Patient safety, ethical frameworks, and user behavior must be considered in the clinical integration of AI-based systems.

items.title: Creative entrepreneurship as a socially embedded form of work: a sociological ecology for the platform society
items.abstract: Creative entrepreneurship increasingly combines creative production with entrepreneurial, communicative, and platform-mediated work. Existing scholarship has generated important insights into opportunity recognition, innovation, value creation, and creative labor, but these perspectives often examine entrepreneurial activity, social relations, cultural recognition, and platform governance as analytically separate processes. This Perspective develops the Sociological Ecology of Creative Entrepreneurship (SECE), a conceptual framework that positions creative entrepreneurship as socially embedded work within platform society. Drawing on economic sociology, sociology of work, labor process theory, digital sociology, and platform studies, SECE integrates five analytically distinct but relationally connected dimensions: identity construction, relational capital, platform governance, cultural legitimacy, and institutional embeddedness. The framework is presented as a relational and multilevel heuristic rather than a tested causal model. It proposes that creative entrepreneurial practice emerges through interactions among workers, audiences, collaborators, platforms, cultural fields, and institutions. The Perspective further considers how these relations are shaped by power, inequality, and human–AI interaction and identifies directions for empirical research into platform-mediated creative work, occupational sustainability, and changing forms of employment.

items.title: CSIR: Contextually and Socially Informed Robots for Efficient Person Goal Navigation
items.abstract: We address the Person Goal Navigation (PersonNav) problem, enabling robots to search for people under realistic constraints on information accessibility and language uncertainty. This tackles the current solutions revolving around rigid person finding systems requiring exact knowledge of the individual for item-delivery in indoor settings. While the focus in literature is on learned methods using unavailable public or sparse data due to human privacy. We propose a planning framework that combines distance and semantic information about the recipient (habits and intent) weighted by the trust of the user-provided information. A synthetic benchmark of scenarios is also developed including actors, items, and requests to evaluate performance before real-world deployment aiming to simulate natural language human-robot interactions. Results show our informed search outperforms classical distance-based graph baselines, while semantics alone lead to ungrounded, sporadic search. Our method achieves strong gains over baselines, with an LLM-based variant performing comparably, and its explicit belief representation naturally supports future Bayesian filtering. Hardware tests demonstrate our method supports real-world embodiment able to leverage between semantic and distance information in a real setting. This work moves toward more intelligent mobile service agents capable of human-like, informed search in realistic environments to be leveraged in day-to-day use. https://anonymous.4open.science/r/personnavsite-4ED2/index.html.

items.title: CuBEs: Culturally-Situated Behavioral Evaluations and the Limitations of Culture-Blind LLM Judges
items.abstract: Evaluating the occurrence and triggers of large language model (LLM) behaviors - such as sycophancy, self-preference, or over-confidence - is critical for predicting real-world model deployment risks. However, existing situated behavioral evaluations typically ignore cultural context, limiting their generalizability across an increasingly global user base. To address this gap, we propose CuBEs - Culturally-situated Behavior Evaluations that probe for response patterns across diverse user cultures. We first extend an automated testing pipeline to inject cultural context into behavioral test scenarios and subsequent evaluation. We assess the cultural adaptability of this pipeline by building a human-labeled dataset that captures nuanced dimensions of behavior understanding across 12 distinct cultures. Our dataset reveals significant cross-cultural variations that one-size-fits all judgments fail to capture. Through evaluating 13 open- and closed-source LLMs, we find that introducing cultural situatedness in the evaluation scenario creates significant variation in the presence of a behavior. For example, while our baseline experiments testing for political bias capture localized Western political dimensions like the American conservative-progressive divide, non-Western culturally situated evaluations surface entirely different axes of bias such as religious and colonial political issues. Our findings demonstrate that standard, culturally-agnostic evaluations fail to capture these shifts, highlighting the necessity of culturally situated behavioral testing for global deployments.

items.title: Data availability and FAIRness in intervention studies on oral mucositis in children and adolescents: a meta-research study
items.abstract: This meta-research study will assess the availability and FAIRness (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) of data supporting the primary outcomes of intervention studies on oral mucositis in children and adolescents (0–19 years). Oral mucositis is a painful and common complication of chemotherapy, head and neck radiotherapy, and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation conditioning. It can affect eating, speaking, infection risk, and cancer treatment itself. Data sharing in dentistry has been shown to be rare, but no study has yet assessed it in pediatric oral mucositis research specifically. We will run a systematic search, with no language or date restrictions, of MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, Web of Science, LILACS, and ProQuest Dissertations & Theses. We will include prospective intervention studies, randomized or non-randomized, in which at least one primary outcome relates to oral mucositis. Screening, data extraction, and all assessments will be performed independently by one human reviewer and a generative AI tool (Claude, Anthropic) acting as second reviewer, with disagreements resolved by a third human reviewer. For each study, we will classify both declared and effective data availability, including the data availability statement, access route, repository, identifier, license, and documentation. When data are "available on request," we will contact the authors in a standardized way. We will assess located datasets that have a persistent identifier or resolvable URL using the automated F-UJI tool. Risk of bias (RoB 2 / ROBINS-I) and discrepancies between registered and reported primary outcomes will be explored as secondary aims. The study will not synthesize clinical effects. We expect to estimate the proportion of studies with complete, partial, or no effective data availability and to describe the FAIRness levels of the datasets we locate, including differences between publication periods (up to 2015 vs. 2016 onward). The findings should show where data transparency and responsible reuse can be improved in pediatric oral mucositis research.

items.title: Data Privacy Concerns and Consumer Engagement with AI-Enabled Global Digital Platforms in Bangladesh: The Mediating Role of Perceived Trust
items.abstract: This study examines how data privacy concerns shape consumer engagement with AI-enabled global digital platforms in Bangladesh and tests perceived trust as an intervening mechanism. The study responds to the rapid normalization of data-intensive platform services in an emerging digital economy, where privacy concern, trust and continued participation coexist rather than operate as simple opposites. A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was used. Of 400 database rows, 385 complete cases passed the embedded attention check and were retained. Privacy concern, perceived trust and consumer engagement were measured with three five-point Likert items each. Composite-score regression and non-parametric bootstrap mediation were used as a transparent robustness-oriented analysis because the three-item scales displayed only modest internal consistency. Privacy concern was positively associated with trust (b=0.164, p=0.006); trust, in turn, was positively associated with engagement while controlling for privacy concern (b=0.231, p<.001). The total privacy-concern-engagement association was small but significant (b=0.117, p=0.026), whereas the direct effect became non-significant after trust entered the model (b=0.079, p=0.123). The bootstrapped indirect effect was 0.038, 95% CI [0.010, 0.072], indicating an indirect pathway through trust. These results reveal a contextually important privacy-trust-engagement configuration, but the modest reliability of the short scales requires cautious interpretation. The article therefore contributes both substantive evidence and a measurement lesson for platform research in Bangladesh: privacy salience may coexist with engagement when users retain confidence in established platforms, yet stronger validated measures are needed before definitive causal or theory-confirming claims are made. items.title: DataWeave: Deploying Human-LLM Analytics for Exploratory Structured Data Analysis
items.abstract: Data journalism, the practice of using data analysis to surface newsworthy stories, depends increasingly on the ability of reporters and investigative journalists to uncover trends, disparities, and accountability narratives. In practice, exploring large structured datasets remains slow and brittle: journalists must navigate hundreds of variables across many datasets over years, understand data coding conventions, and write non-trivial analysis code while hypotheses evolve. Although LLMs are often touted as "ask in English, get SQL/answers," real newsroom workflows expose recurring failures, e.g., schema mismatches and drift, misread domain semantics and units, and silent assumptions. We present DataWeave, a system that addresses these needs by combining conversational interaction, schema grounding, analytical planning, and executable query generation to support exploratory analysis over structured data. Rather than treating LLMs as autonomous answer engines, DataWeave frames them as interactive partners whose outputs can be inspected, corrected, and steered as hypotheses shift. We present a case study with professional journalists using our system to analyze the U.S. Department of Education's Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS), a high-stakes public dataset with substantial domain semantics and frequent schema updates. We also report how deployment experience and iterative refinement shaped the current DataWeave architecture and its analytical workflow. Our findings distill design principles and deployment lessons for trustworthy human-LLM collaboration in structured data analysis.

items.title: Decision-Focused Sensor Network Placement for Rapid Disaster Response
items.abstract: Timely and reliable decision-making is critical for disaster emergency response, yet it is fundamentally constrained by limited situational awareness due to sparse and imperfect sensing under budget and data accessibility constraints. In current practice, flood management systems follow a two-stage pipeline that separately reconstructs and predicts flood states from sparse sensor observations, and then optimizes downstream response decisions, such as evacuation planning and resource allocation. However, existing approaches typically adopt decision-agnostic strategies for both sensor placement (e.g., maximizing information gain) and model training (e.g., minimizing average prediction error), neglecting the inherent mismatch between sensing effectiveness or predictive accuracy and decision quality. As a result, systems with similar sensing performance or forecasting errors can yield substantially different decisions. To address this limitation, we propose a decision-focused learning (DFL) framework for sensor-aware flood monitoring and response optimization. First, we formulate sensor placement and flood forecasting as a unified decision-informed learning problem, where sensing, prediction, and optimization are tightly coupled. Second, we train the reconstruction and forecasting model to directly minimize downstream decision regret, enabling end-to-end alignment between prediction and optimization objectives. Third, to handle the heterogeneous optimization structures in the pipeline, namely discrete combinatorial sensor selection under hard budget constraints and structured downstream decision-making, we develop a hybrid DFL framework that integrates perturbation-based learning via Implicit Maximum Likelihood Estimation (I-MLE) for differentiable sensor selection with surrogate-based decision-focused optimization (SPO+) for decision-aligned model training. Extensive experiments on real-world hurricane and flood scenarios demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently improves downstream decision quality, achieving lower regret compared to prediction-focused baselines. These results highlight the importance of decision-aware sensing and provide a principled approach for integrating sensor placement, forecasting, and optimization in disaster response systems.

items.title: Decoding Figurative Language in Journalism Translation: Human and LLM Translation of English-Vietnamese Metaphors
items.abstract: The increasing use of large language models (LLMs) in professional translation has reshaped multilingual news production. While prior research has reported gains in fluency and surface-level accuracy, limited attention has been paid to LLMs’ ability to translate figurative language, which plays a key role in meaning construction and evaluative stance in journalistic discourse. This study investigates the extent to which state-of-the-art LLMs achieve functional and cultural equivalence in the English–Vietnamese translation of journalistic metaphors, in comparison with professional human translators. Adopting a mixed-methods comparative design, the study analyzes a purposively selected corpus of 50 metaphorical sentences from major international news outlets. Translation outputs produced by two LLMs (GPT-4o and Claude 3.5) under two prompting conditions (zero-shot and advanced prompting) were compared with a human benchmark generated by senior Vietnamese news editors. All translations were evaluated through blind expert assessment based on four criteria: semantic accuracy, naturalness, cultural equivalence, and journalistic style. The findings show that advanced prompting significantly improves AI performance, particularly in semantic accuracy and stylistic fluency. However, LLMs continue to underperform in cultural equivalence, often exhibiting literalism and reduced metaphorical resonance. These findings underscore the indispensable role of human expertise as cultural and pragmatic mediators, suggesting that while LLMs accelerate production, human transcreation remains essential to preserving the rhetorical integrity of multilingual journalism.

items.title: Decoupling Memory from Context: Structured Memory for Token-Efficient Test-Time Continual Learning
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in enterprise, scientific, and medical applications, where agents must incorporate domain-specific knowledge and adapt from experience. Context engineering offers a practical alternative to weight updates by improving model behavior through instructions, strategies, and evidence supplied at inference time. However, adapting context online typically requires a costly trial-and-error process, while queries are often processed independently, preventing useful experience from carrying forward. Memory systems address this limitation by retaining information across interactions, but approaches that continually append information to a shared context face increasing token costs, context-window limits, and performance degradation as the context expands. We introduce a unified formulation of context optimization and show that an agent memory system update can be interpreted as an optimization update procedure over the model's context. This perspective attempts to provide a principled framework for studying memory design and its efficiency. We then propose GraphMemory, a lightweight graph-based memory that accumulates, refines, organizes, and connects reusable strategies. For each query, GraphMemory retrieves only the relevant subgraph, enabling online context adaptation without exposing the model to the entire memory. Under bounded retrieval, the amount of retrieved memory remains constant as the number of processed examples grows. Experiments show that GraphMemory achieves competitive downstream performance while using approximately 81-85% fewer memory-construction tokens than our baselines.

items.title: Deepfake Image Detection Using Squeeze-and-Excitation Attention and Adaptive Threshold Optimization
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) has significantly improved the realism of manipulated facial images and videos, creating serious risks for social-network misinformation, content security, and digital trust. This study focuses on visual deepfake image detection rather than multimodal misinformation detection. Existing convolutional neural network (CNN)-based deepfake detectors commonly rely on a fixed decision threshold of 0.5, which may be unstable when facial images are affected by compression, cropping, noise, and distribution shifts in practical social-media environments. To improve detection reliability, this paper proposes a lightweight deepfake image detection framework that integrates a CNN backbone, a Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention module, and an adaptive threshold optimization strategy. The key novelty of this work is not conventional threshold tuning alone, but a lightweight detection framework that jointly combines SE-based channel-wise feature recalibration, F1-score-driven adaptive threshold optimization, and leakage-aware group-level evaluation. Compared with post-hoc threshold tuning or calibration methods that mainly adjust the output boundary after training, the proposed framework improves both forgery-sensitive feature representation and the final classification decision mechanism. Specifically, the SE module enhances forgery-related feature representation through channel-wise feature recalibration, while the adaptive threshold is selected according to the F1-score, which is the harmonic mean of precision and recall. A group-level data split is also adopted to ensure that frames from the same video are not shared across the training, validation, and test sets, thereby reducing identity leakage. Experiments are conducted on a FaceForensics++-derived dataset using multiple CNN backbones and five-fold cross-validation. The evaluation metrics include accuracy, F1-score, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC), and the area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC). The results show that threshold optimization improves the ResNet18 baseline accuracy from 0.8835 ± 0.0186 to 0.9016 ± 0.0151 and the F1-score from 0.8773 ± 0.0253 to 0.9042 ± 0.0138. Among the tested backbones, ResNet50 achieves the best cross-validation performance, with an accuracy of 0.9061 ± 0.0161 and a ROC-AUC of 0.9680 ± 0.0075. Under the strict group-level test setting, the proposed framework achieves 0.9960 accuracy and 0.9959 F1-score on the constructed test set. Compared with more complex detection pipelines. The proposed method is simple, computationally practical, and easy to integrate into common CNN-based deepfake detectors. Therefore, this work provides a practical visual security detection approach for social-media content verification and cyber-security applications.

items.title: Defense-in-Depth at the Perception-Reasoning Interface of LLM-Centric Agentic UAV Swarms
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly support Uncrewed Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarm operations such as data collection scheduling, where the model reads structured sensor reports and decides which sensors to visit. An adversary who quietly manipulates those reports can redirect the swarm without modifying the model weights or the UAV. Defenses for this interface have been proposed architecturally but rarely implemented or evaluated. We implement and evaluate defense-in-depth at the perception-reasoning interface of LLM-Centric Agentic UAV Swarms. Five layers check the provenance of a report, whether its values are physically admissible, whether they agree with what swarm geometry and service history predict, whether the resulting schedule starves any sensor, and, when these fail, hand control to a deterministic scheduler that ignores the suspect input. We test each layer against an adversary strong enough to defeat the layer before it. For each of the three input-side layers, we derive in closed form how far a report can be distorted before that layer reacts, fixing each boundary from deployment parameters before any attack data is collected; across thirty matched simulation runs, predicted and measured boundaries agree. Separating attack detection from response is a well-established principle, and we quantify the cost of neglecting this distinction at the perception-reasoning interface. When the system rejects a report, it replaces it with the most recent accepted report. This prevents the adversary from controlling the UAV schedule, but it also increases cumulative cost by 79% and 74% for the two detectors, respectively, compared with the undefended system. The safety check does not detect any attacks, but it nevertheless reduces the attack-induced cost by 37.5%.

items.title: Demographic-Adjusted Normative Equations for the Oculo-Cognitive Addition Test (OCAT): A Foundation for Individualized Oculo-Cognitive Assessment
items.abstract: Background: Many neurological and cognitive disorders have early oculomotor hallmarks. The Oculo-Cognitive Addition Test (OCAT) is a quick, objective screening tool that measures eye movement and time-based biomarkers of cognitive processing during simple mental addition tasks in under two minutes. Normative values for age, sex, education level, and apolipoprotein E Type 4 (APOE ε4) carrier status must be established so cognitively normal populations are not misdiagnosed. Methods: A total of 382 participants completed OCAT, with 350 participants making up the normative cohort from which raw gaze data were processed to derive fixations, saccades, blinks, pupillary dynamics, and time-based features. Separate multiple linear regression models were fitted for each feature with age, sex, education, and APOE ε4 carrier status as predictors to establish demographic-adjusted normative equations. Results: Processing time, fixation time, fixation size and fixation area and their variability increased progressively from the first to the third number within each addition sequence, consistent with increasing cognitive workload. Demographic-adjusted multiple linear regression models generated normative equations for individual OCAT features based on age, sex, education, and APOE ε4 carrier status. These models were used to derive individualized expected values, 95% reference intervals, and z-scores. Conclusions: These demographic-adjusted normative equations enable individualized interpretation of OCAT performance and are necessary steps towards clinical implementation.

items.title: Dependable AI-Assisted Engineering: A Formal Framework for AI Participation and Assurance in Safety-Critical Workflows
items.abstract: Generative AI can produce engineering artefacts, but generation alone does not determine whether or how those artefacts should enter safety-critical workflows. This paper develops a formal framework for assigning AI participation and assurance at the level of individual workflow units. Each unit has a participation and assurance record covering its engineering requirement, an approved operational formalization where applicable, the applicable mechanism, fallback where applicable, evidence obligations and the applicable guarantee, plus a deployment-readiness status. The framework distinguishes deterministic verification, statistically calibrated admission, authorized human judgement supported by AI advice, authorized human adjudication of AI-produced artefacts, retained deterministic tool paths and explicit non-participation; these arrangements carry different kinds of guarantee rather than levels on a common scale. The framework also separates formalization fidelity from verifier soundness, provides a staged classification and readiness procedure, and derives conditions for comparing a gated AI-assisted unit with an incumbent process under recurring-population assumptions. We instantiate and apply the framework in an executed 17-unit wing-spar structural-analysis workflow combining deterministically gated AI-generated CAD, retained deterministic computation and human judgement. The AI-generated CAD program passed all 23 deterministic checks and was admitted at the first attempt. Favourable stress magnitudes did not suffice to pass the stress criteria where the predeclared mesh-convergence evidence was insufficient; those criteria were instead referred to engineering judgement. The case demonstrates selective AI participation and explicit evidence handling at unit level; no claim is made of workflow-level dependability, certification, structural safety or productivity.

items.title: Dependency Restructuring: How Technological Enactment Changes Organizational Requirement Relations
items.abstract: Digital technologies can change organizational work without changing the dependencies through which work is coordinated. This article examines the cases in which those dependencies do change. Dependency restructuring is defined as a change in what organizational activities require from one another, or from technological and external providers, after a technology is put into use. The analysis separates changes in activities from changes in dependencies and from the coordination needed to manage them. Individual dependency relations may be created, eliminated, or redirected to a different provider; previously separate sets of dependencies may also become connected. Two conditional propositions follow from this distinction. The first concerns situations in which local autonomy increases while reliance on a shared technological or external capability also increases. The second concerns situations in which different technologies produce similar coordination requirements because they generate similar dependency configurations under similar organizational conditions. Two evidence-based illustrations—enterprise cloud migration and artificial-intelligence integration in organizational workflows—show how the approach can be applied without treating the cases as tests of the theory. The result is a bounded meso-level account of when technological enactment changes what organizational activities require, from whom or from what, and how those changes affect coordination.

items.title: Design and Expert-Based Usability Evaluation of a Smart Mobile Application for Aphasia Rehabilitation
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: This paper aims to develop an artificial intelligence-assisted mobile application using speech recognition and image processing technologies to address language difficulties experienced by individuals with aphasia. Methods: The mobile application was developed in the Android Studio environment using the Java programming language. Google Speech API was used for speech recognition, and Google ML Kit’s image labelling APIs were used for image recognition. The development process of the application was conducted using the Scrum methodology. Features developed during the sprints for each module were evaluated through Expectation Tests conducted with expert participation. In these tests, users’ pre-application expectations and post-application experiences with the modules were analysed through comparison. At the end of the development process, a System Usability Scale (SUS) Test was conducted to assess the overall integration of all modules. Results: Based on the results of Expectation Tests, necessary updates were made, and improvements were implemented in the functionality of each module. According to the SUS Test results, the application demonstrated an acceptable level of usability rate, and positive feedback was received in terms of user experience. The expert evaluation indicated that the application has acceptable usability and shows promise as a supportive tool for aphasia rehabilitation. Conclusions: This prototype application has the potential to support speech skills of individuals with aphasia, especially those who face challenges in accessing a Speech and Language Therapist. The integration of artificial intelligence-supported speech recognition and image processing technologies offers a promising supportive tool for the language rehabilitation of individuals with aphasia. Testing this prototype with a wider group of users and continuously updating it will be crucial in providing further support to individuals with aphasia.

items.title: Design and Open-Water Validation of an Autonomous Underwater Robot for Physical Diver Safety Assistance
items.abstract: Diving accidents remain frequently fatal, and most stem from preventable human factors: panic, failed buoyancy control, and disorientation. Underwater human–robot interaction research has focused on observing the diver and offers little help when a diver must be pulled to safety. This paper presents the design and sea validation of NADIA, an autonomous underwater robot that combines diver guidance and following with diver-commanded physical assistance. A rear handle converts the diver’s grip into thrust and springs back to neutral on release; a diver-facing display shows depth, distance, battery state, and warnings. Six vector thrusters, with mounting angles optimized by gradient descent against drag-model thrust-ratio targets, are driven by an operational-space time-delay controller (TDC-OSF) that keeps the robot in the diver’s view; stereo vision and imaging sonar are fused for diver detection. In test-bed, tank, and sea trials, surge and heave thrusts matched design targets within 5–7%; approval-gated guidance held the robot 1–2 m from the diver with position and heading errors below 0.15 m and 3.5°; and the robot towed a diver at about 1 m/s and rose from 5 m to the surface in about 4 s. An underwater robot can thus serve as a physical safety layer for divers.

items.title: Designing Lunar Habitats for Long-Term Human Exploration: Insights From a Product Design Perspective
items.abstract: Deep space exploration research seeks to support long-term human presence on the Moon through innovative habitat solutions. Research on lunar habitats emphasises the need for integrated socio-technical solutions addressing extreme environmental conditions and human factors challenges through interdisciplinary design approaches. However, existing research mainly focuses on architectural and engineering perspectives, while product design frameworks for space product innovation remain fragmented. This paper investigates how product design approaches, methods, and tools can contribute to the development of habitable space infrastructures through a Research through Design strategy. The paper focuses on the integrated application of the Double-Diamond Design Thinking Model, Human-Centred Design and Human Systems Integration research phases and tasks to address the Space It Up! project research challenges on designing habitation means, crew stations, and logistics modules. The proposed framework is demonstrated through the development of the space-exploration habitat system strategic brief and the Moon Mobile Habitation concept, highlighting how the integrated framework, modelling and codesign approaches, and interdisciplinary collaboration translate human, operational, and system requirements into product design scenarios. The paper contributes a scalable methodological framework that systematises design phases, tasks, methods, and tools to support interdisciplinary collaboration and innovation for human-centred, mission-driven, and system-oriented space infrastructures.

items.title: Designing the Future of User Feedback for Generative AI
items.abstract: Post-deployment feedback from users can be a cost-effective, scalable, and representative means to monitor and improve generative AI systems and features. When implemented effectively, giving such feedback can increase users' engagement with and trust in GenAI systems. Government regulations and industry guidelines call for post-deployment user engagement, but there is little guidance on designing mechanisms that are usable for consumers and provide actionable input for product teams. We conducted a multi-phase study as a collaboration between academic researchers and eBay. Our benchmark evaluation of current industry approaches identified common issues including lack of discoverability, unclear terminology, and inattention to user value. Based on these findings, we developed best-practice recommendations and designed and tested a prototype feedback-collection tool. The tool aimed to provide users with an efficient, flexible, and positive feedback-giving experience, and provide product teams with rich data on performance and potential problems in a usable format.

items.title: Developing a Socratic Artificial Intelligence Tutor Using Retrieval Augmented Generation and Pedagogical Prompting
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) applications such as ChatGPT present a distinct challenge for computer science (CS) students. While they offer individualized learning support, unregulated use risks facilitating academic shortcuts and eroding critical thinking skills. This article introduces Lion-AI, a chatbot tutor developed to augment the CS educational experience. Lion-AI integrates retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), rooted in university-specific course materials, with an engineered Socratic interaction policy. Unlike general-use tools, Lion-AI is designed to classify student requests, redirect direct-solution requests through diagnostic questioning, and provide guidance through one-question-at a-time interaction. The study describes a method for creating ethically constrained AI tutors in CS education. It presents the system’s three-tier architecture, the RAG pipeline, and the transparent interaction policy behind the tutor, positioning Lion-AI as a deployable proof of concept for combining curriculum grounding with explicit Socratic constraints. A controlled classroom study is planned as the next step.

items.title: Development and Validation of Human-AI Collaborative Workflow in SNOMED CT Mapping of Bilingual Clinical Text
items.abstract: Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine-Clinical Terminology (SNOMED CT) is the principal international standard for semantic interoperability of clinical information, but mapping free-text clinical narratives to SNOMED CT concepts remains labor-intensive. We developed a large language model agent system for mapping bilingual clinical text to SNOMED CT concepts and evaluated its effect on mapping accuracy and efficiency within a human-AI collaborative workflow. We designed a three-module agent system comprising translation, abbreviation expansion, and vector-based retrieval components, integrated with a pre-embedded SNOMED CT vector database. Three health information managers independently mapped bilingual clinical text segments using three approaches: human-only, Agent-only, and Agent-assisted human mapping. Performance was evaluated by using hit rate, precision, recall, and F1 score at k = 1 and 5, and R-precision. Mapping time was compared between human-only and human-AI collaborative approaches. A total of 2,261 de-identified clinical text segments across nine clinical categories were collected at a tertiary academic hospital in South Korea. The human-AI collaborative workflow, which expanded the set of valid SNOMED CT candidates presented at each mapping decision, raised pooled hit rate@1 from 0.837 to 0.868 (difference 0.031, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.021 to 0.042; p < 0.001), raised R-precision from 0.632 to 0.674 (difference 0.042, 95% CI 0.034 to 0.051; p < 0.001), and reduced total mapping time by 53.9% (from 1.57 to 0.72 min per segment, including agent processing). By expanding the space of valid SNOMED CT candidates available to expert mappers, the human-AI collaborative approach improved SNOMED CT mapping accuracy while reducing time by about half. Its modular architecture, supporting periodic vector database updates without retraining, offers a sustainable and efficient solution for bilingual clinical terminology standardization.

items.title: Differences in prevalence and predictive value of metabolic syndrome
items.abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is common in Chinese adults, but evidence regarding its burden and cardiovascular relevance among young healthcare workers (HCWs) remains limited. Different MetS definitions can yield materially different prevalence estimates and risk classifications. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 420 HCWs aged 20 to 45 years who underwent mandatory annual health examinations at a tertiary hospital in China from 2022 to 2024. Demographic, occupational, anthropometric, and biochemical data were extracted from health examination and personnel records. MetS was defined using the International Diabetes Federation (IDF), revised National Cholesterol Education Program Adult Treatment Panel III (NCEP ATP III), and Chinese Diabetes Society (CDS) criteria. Ten-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk was estimated using the China-PAR equations, with elevated estimated risk defined as ≥10%. We compared MetS prevalence, sex differences, agreement among definitions, diagnostic performance using NCEP ATP III. Participants had a mean age of 32.4 ± 5.8 years, and 30.0% were men. MetS prevalence was 15.5%, 18.6%, and 10.2% according to IDF, NCEP ATP III, and CDS criteria, respectively, and was consistently higher in men. Agreement was almost perfect between IDF and NCEP ATP III (κ = 0.82) and substantial between IDF and CDS (κ = 0.64) and between NCEP ATP III and CDS (κ = 0.61). Using an internally reconstructed 2 × 2 table that preserves the reported prevalence counts and pairwise κ values, IDF showed sensitivity 78.2%, specificity 98.8%, PPV 93.8%, and NPV 95.2%, whereas CDS showed sensitivity 51.3%, specificity 99.1%, PPV 93.0%, and NPV 89.9% relative to NCEP ATP III. These reconstructed diagnostic-performance values require verification against the original participant-level data before submission. MetS defined by any criterion was strongly associated with elevated China-PAR-estimated risk, with adjusted odds ratio of 6.5, 7.1, and 5.1 for IDF, NCEP ATP III, and CDS, respectively. atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease-risk AUCs were 0.80, 0.82, and 0.76, respectively. In this single-center cohort of young Chinese HCWs, estimated MetS prevalence differed substantially by diagnostic definition. IDF and NCEP ATP III identified more cases than CDS and showed stronger mutual agreement. The observed associations with China-PAR-estimated risk support the potential value of MetS assessment within occupational health screening.

items.title: Digital competence, artificial intelligence utilization, and innovation capability: Basis for a maritime technology adoption framework for Filipino seafarers
items.abstract: This study assessed the digital competence, artificial intelligence utilization, and innovation capability of Filipino seafarers and proposed a Maritime Technology Adoption Framework.The study employed a quantitative descriptive-correlational research design, and 384 Filipino seafarers were selected using purposive sampling.Data were gathered through a structured questionnaire adapted from the DigComp Framework, contemporary maritime artificial intelligence utilization models, and innovation capability frameworks.The results revealed that Filipino seafarers demonstrated a high level of digital competence (CM = 3.55), with Information Literacy obtaining the highest assessment.Likewise, respondents exhibited a high extent of artificial intelligence utilization (CM = 3.79), with the Human Element dimension receiving the highest rating, highlighting the continued importance of human judgment in AIassisted operations.Furthermore, Filipino seafarers showed a high level of innovation capability (CM = 3.68), with Performance emerging as the highest-rated dimension.Correlation analysis indicated significant relationships between selected dimensions of digital competence and artificial intelligence utilization, as well as between selected dimensions of artificial intelligence utilization and innovation capability.However, no significant relationship was found between digital competence and innovation capability.A framework for Maritime Technology Adoption for Filipino Seafarers was developed based on the findings of the study.The framework identifies Digital Competence as the foundation, Artificial Intelligence Utilization as the enabling mechanism, and Innovation Capability as the outcome, highlighting both the direct and indirect pathways through which digital competence strengthens innovation capability.The framework provides a structured guide for workforce readiness and maritime digital transformation.

items.title: Digital Transformation in Commerce & Business Management: Emerging Trends and Future Prospects
items.abstract: Digital transformation has emerged as a fundamental driver of change in commerce and business management, reshaping how organisations operate, compete, and create value. The integration of technologies such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, big data analytics, blockchain, Internet of Things, automation, and digital payment systems has transformed traditional business models and consumer interactions. This paper examines the emerging trends in digital transformation and evaluates their implications for commerce and business management. It focuses on the increasing adoption of e-commerce, data-driven decision-making, intelligent automation, personalised customer experiences, digital supply chains, and platform-based business models. The study also considers challenges related to cybersecurity, data privacy, digital skills, technological costs, and organisational resistance to change. Further, it explores future prospects associated with artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, immersive technologies, and sustainable digital business practices. The paper highlights the need for organisations to develop adaptive strategies, technological capabilities, and digitally skilled human resources to achieve sustainable growth in an increasingly technology-driven business environment

items.title: Digital Trust under Autonomous AI and Quantum Risk: Signed Memory, Cryptographic Unpredictability, and Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later
items.abstract: Governments are adopting artificial intelligence at the same moment that the cryptographic assumptions under their long-lived secrets are being placed on a clock. This paper treats four developments as a single problem of digital trust rather than as separate technical topics. First, AI systems are moving from content generation to agentic action, and are already exposed to impersonation, poisoning and unauthorised use. Second, persistent memory across sessions creates a new class of institutional record, whose integrity cannot be reduced to a signature. Third, cryptographic security depends on unpredictable keys, not on non-determinism, and better randomness does not answer a quantum attack on public-key mathematics. Fourth, harvest-now-decrypt-later means that the threat to data which must remain confidential for decades exists before a cryptographically relevant quantum computer does. Drawing on published resource estimates, the NIST post-quantum standards, and the positions of major security agencies on quantum key distribution, the paper argues that preparation should begin with an inventory of vulnerable cryptography, hybrid migration of high-value key exchange, and an explicit regime for the ownership and correction of AI memory. The implications for diplomatic communications and for states with constrained compute and language resources are developed throughout. items.title: Divergence controls entropy in distillation
items.abstract: Distillation has become a core primitive of large language model training, but its properties are not yet well understood. We take an entropic perspective, studying how the entropy of the student depends on the data and the divergence that define the distillation objective. We prove that forward KL inflates the entropy of the student above that of the teacher. Since cross-entropy training is a special case, this yields an identity that we verify quantitatively in pretraining and supervised finetuning. Other divergences come with no such guarantee: reverse KL deflates entropy until the gap between student and teacher gets too large, and interpolating between the two changes entropy smoothly early in training but abruptly at convergence. The lower entropy of on-policy distillation comes from token-level reverse KL, not from on-policy sampling. The divergence therefore acts as an implicit entropy regularizer, whose role is clearest in self-distillation: as conditioning on privileged information deflates entropy, the divergence hyperparameters that work best are those that compensate for it.

items.title: DNAlign: Dynamic Null-Space Safe Alignment for LLMs
items.abstract: Ensuring the safe and reliable deployment of large language models (LLMs) remains a fundamental challenge. Existing safety alignment approaches either incur high computational cost or unintentionally disrupt the model's core knowledge, leading to degraded fluency and factual accuracy on benign tasks. This reveals a persistent trade-off between safety and utility. We propose DNAlign, a lightweight alignment framework that integrates control-theoretic optimization with null-space projection. By treating the LLM as a dynamic system, the proposed framework introduces controllable perturbations to steer generation toward safe behavior. A key component is the projection module, which restricts these perturbations to the harmful-related subspace derived from neutral hidden states, thereby preserving general knowledge and response quality. A value function trained on human preference data adaptively optimizes the control signals to align with human safety preferences. Extensive evaluations across multiple LLM backbones demonstrate that our framework consistently reduces harmful outputs while maintaining fluency, coherence, and factual utility. It achieves superior overall performance compared to prior alignment baselines without sacrificing generation diversity. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides an effective and practically deployable solution for safe LLM alignment. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DNAlign.

items.title: Do Large Language Models Know Colombian Law? A Reliability Benchmark for the Colombian Legal System
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support legal practice, education, and research, yet their reliability in national legal systems outside the United States remains largely undocumented. We introduce an expert-validated benchmark for evaluating LLM reliability on the Colombian legal system. The benchmark comprises 1,042 items spanning ten areas of law and three question formats (closed multiple-choice, semi-open, and open-ended IRAC), built through a human-in-the-loop pipeline with multi-stage expert review. We evaluate 15 contemporary proprietary and open-weight models with format-appropriate metrics. Accuracy on closed questions ranges widely, from 0.905 (Gemini 3.1 Pro) to 0.577, but on free-text legal answers factual correctness never exceeds 0.45 (on a 0-1 scale) for any model. We find a dissociation between answer relevancy and correctness (Spearman rho = -0.46): models reliably sound responsive while frequently being wrong, a pattern of particular concern for non-expert users. Closed-question accuracy and free-text correctness are strongly rank-correlated (rho = 0.94), so cheap multiple-choice screening predicts model ranking but overstates absolute reliability. An independent rubric-based LLM judge and blind human expert scoring both reproduce the free-text ranking (rho >= 0.88). The judge further reveals that only about half of the norms models cite are correct; the rest are wrong or non-existent. items.title: Does Shared Reading Promote Cognitive Development? A Literature Review
items.abstract: Shared reading is recognized as an educational method that promotes language development and emergent literacy during early childhood. However, growing evidence suggests that it influences additional developmental domains. This review examined empirical and theoretical literature with the aim of uncovering the potential of shared reading as an inclusive pedagogical approach for supporting children’s cognitive development by integrating findings on adult mediation, dialogic interaction, repeated reading, mental state discourse, instructional adaptations, and shared reading across diverse learner populations. The reviewed literature indicates that the effectiveness of shared reading depends primarily on the quality of the adult–child interaction. Adult mediation, instructional scaffolding, collaborative dialogue, and active child participation were found to be key instruments for supporting learning across home, preschool, and inclusive educational settings. Studies involving children with developmental disabilities, autism spectrum disorder, deafness, and deafblindness indicate that adapted shared reading promotes participation and advances language, communication, and broader developmental outcomes. Significant conceptual, methodological, and population-related gaps were found. Furthermore, few studies examined the contribution of shared reading to higher-order cognitive processes, such as executive functions, metacognition, inferential reasoning, cognitive flexibility, and critical thinking. Research on culturally and linguistically diverse populations, particularly Arabic-speaking learners, is also limited. This review proposes a reconceptualization of shared reading as an inclusive cognitive pedagogy in which adult mediation, dialogic interaction, instructional scaffolding, and collaborative meaning-making together promote children’s cognitive engagement and higher-order thinking.

items.title: DyadMem: A Long-Term Memory Benchmark of How Agents Work with Users
items.abstract: Long-term agents must remember not only what is true about a user, but also how a particular agent should work with that user as their shared history evolves. Existing benchmarks primarily supervise user facts and preferences or experience reusable across users, leaving this relationship-specific agent memory implicit. Additionally, most prior works measure the model solely with final-answer QA over long interaction histories, making the assessment still incomplete and unreliable. To this end, we introduce DyadMem with the proposed new definition User-conditioned Relational Agent Memory (URAM). DyadMem jointly annotates user-side memory and URAM along the same multi-session trajectories, resulting in 6 memory categories. To summarize, it includes 3,065 episodes, 50,961 sessions, and 61,210 QA instances, with extensive session-level Capture and Update gold annotations, query-level Recall support, and two QA settings: Gold-Memory and Full-Pipeline. Across 16 open-weight and 4 proprietary models, Gold-Memory QA is consistently strong, yet Full-Pipeline QA drops sharply. Such a gap explicitly supports our fine-grained evaluation design. Additionally, several quantitative results further reveal low Capture recall, incomplete Recall, and unsafe-deletion issues arising from even the frontier LLMs. We further conduct a rigorous experiment to validate the effectiveness of our URAM and observe the positive effects for all 20 models. In summary, DyadMem is a dual-domain, full-pipeline memory benchmark with extensive annotation efforts for advancing the domain's development.

items.title: ECOPOLITICS IN THE ANTHROPOCENE AND INTERSPECIES SOCIOTECHNICAL DESIGN
items.abstract: This article analyzes counterpoints among cosmopolitics, sympoiesis, ecosocialism, and "degrowth communism" in order to confront the crisis of the Anthropocene with new ways of doing sociotechnical/cosmopolitical design. It offers a critical-analytical literature review that confronts Bruno Latour's Actor-Network Theory, Donna Haraway's figurations, Nancy Fraser's ecosocialist formulations, Kohei Saito's degrowth communism, and Andrew Feenberg's Critical Theory of Technology. It investigates how overcoming modern dualisms and reductionisms enables a new understanding of technology as a field of economic and cosmopolitical dispute. It argues that the redemocratization of technical codes and multispecies justice require abandoning the logic of profit and unlimited growth in favor of an economy oriented toward use value and the sharing of wealth. The complementarity between ecological materialism and sociotechnical design reveals that confronting planetary depletion demands more than isolated engineering solutions; it presupposes a transenvironmental project, but also degrowth, technological democratization, and socio-environmental justice. The article concludes that the process of "staying with the trouble" in the Global South calls for a transformative praxis that integrates institutional re-design with mutual care and territorial solidarity, providing the foundation for a platform of convergence among ecopolitical struggles for the emancipatory co-production of existence.

items.title: EdgeAgent: Orchestrating On-Device LLM inference for End-User Multi-Agent Systems on CPU-GPU Unified Memory Architectures
items.abstract: Emerging multi-agent LLMs demand privacy-preserving edge deployment, yet current inference systems struggle with these collaborative workflows. Specifically, the memory-bound decode phase causes severe bus contention on unified memory architectures (UMA), paralyzing naive CPU-GPU co-execution. Furthermore, speculative decoding in multi-agent workloads faces extreme variance in drafting difficulty, alternating between complex reasoning and predictable structured generation. Compounded by frequent tool-induced stalls, this highly fragmented execution severely underutilizes hardware and defeats traditional static batching. We present EdgeAgent, a cross-layer inference system explicitly co-designed for edge UMA and multi-agent workloads. At the micro-architectural level, it bypasses rigid graph-compiler constraints to enable zero-copy UMA-aware tensor parallelism, utilizing asymmetric memory layouts to fully saturate both CPU and GPU compute units. At the scheduling level, it dynamically allocates draft budgets based on real-time sequence predictability to bound bandwidth waste. Concurrently, an asynchronous suspend-and-yield mechanism actively evicts stalled agents, ensuring continuous hardware saturation during unpredictable tool invocations. Extensive evaluations on an Apple M4 SoC demonstrate that the UMA-aware execution alone contributes a 1.29x speedup over batched speculative decoding. Adding the agent-aware scheduling lifts the full EdgeAgent system to a 1.77x speedup under extreme tool-use latencies.

items.title: Edukasi Dan Penyuluhan Ergonomi Untuk Pencegahan Keluhan Nyeri Punggung Bawah (LBP) Pada Petugas UPT Puskesmas Delitua Kabupaten Deli Serdang
items.abstract: Low Back Pain (LBP) is one of the musculoskeletal problems that may be associated with non-ergonomic working postures. Health center workers may perform their duties in sitting or standing positions for relatively long periods; therefore, adequate understanding of ergonomic practices and LBP prevention is needed. This Community Service (PkM) activity aimed to improve workers’ knowledge and awareness through ergonomic education and health promotion as an effort to prevent LBP at UPT Puskesmas Delitua, Deli Serdang Regency. The activity was conducted through educational sessions, discussions, demonstrations of ergonomic working postures, active breaks, and simple stretching exercises. A total of 65 health workers participated in the activity. Initial identification showed that 35 participants (53.8%) had ergonomic working postures, while 30 participants (46.2%) had non-ergonomic working postures. Based on the initial identification of complaints, 33 participants (50.8%) reported severe LBP symptoms, while 32 participants (49.2%) reported mild symptoms. These initial conditions served as the basis for developing and delivering educational materials covering proper working postures, adjustment of work facilities, implementation of active breaks, and regular stretching exercises. The activity provided participants with an opportunity to understand LBP risk factors and practice the application of more ergonomic working postures in their daily activities. This community service activity is expected to improve workers’ understanding, awareness, and practical skills in applying ergonomic principles as a promotive and preventive effort to reduce the risk of LBP in the workplace.

items.title: EEG-based mental workload recognition during multi-tasking scenarios: the role of resting-state normalization and brain region of EEG features
items.abstract: EEG-based mental workload (MWL) recognition is challenged by inter-individual variability and limited model interpretability. This study investigated MWL recognition in long-term multi-tasking scenarios using resting-state EEG normalisation and regional feature analysis. Participants performed multi-tasking operations at three difficulty levels, while resting-state and task-state EEG, behavioural performance, and NASA-TLX ratings were collected. The best whole-brain model achieved 93.78% ± 0.45% accuracy under standard normalisation, while the parietal configuration retained substantial recognition capability with fewer electrodes. Resting-state normalisation changed EEG feature-importance patterns, but its effects on classification were classifier-dependent rather than uniformly beneficial. SHAP analysis identified prominent frontal and parietal contributions. The findings support interpretable and lightweight EEG-based MWL monitoring in complex operational environments.

items.title: EFFECTIVENESS OF AN AI-BASED METHODOLOGY FOR DEVELOPING ENGLISH ORAL COMMUNICATIVE COMPETENCE AMONG NON-LINGUISTIC UNIVERSITY STUDENTS
items.abstract: This article develops and theoretically substantiates an artificial-intelligence-based methodology for improving the English oral communicative competence of students in non-linguistic higher education institutions. The methodology rests on a Teacher–Learner–AI model in which artificial intelligence serves as a supplementary pedagogical resource rather than a replacement for teachers or authentic human communication. It comprises seven interconnected stages: diagnostic assessment, individualisation, AI-assisted preparation, AI-supported communication, feedback, human interaction, and reflection with reassessment. A quasi-experimental design is proposed for evaluating its effectiveness; the numerical values presented in the article are illustrative and are not offered as actual experimental findings. Oral communicative competence is treated as a five-component construct: linguistic accuracy, fluency, pronunciation and intelligibility, interactional competence, and pragmatic-strategic competence. The study argues that artificial intelligence increases opportunities for meaningful speaking practice only when its use is pedagogically structured and supervised by teachers.

items.title: Efficient Reasoning Training Does Not Always Harm CoT Faithfulness and Monitorability
items.abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning allows humans to inspect how large language models reach their answers, and oversee model behaviour. This reasoning comes at an increased inference cost, motivating efficient methods that train models to solve tasks using fewer tokens. However, a common concern is that such training may cause models to skip important reasoning steps, so the CoT no longer faithfully reflects the model's decision. It is unclear whether or when this occurs in practice, since different efficiency methods apply length pressure to models' CoT in distinct ways, and faithfully explaining a model's decision takes more tokens on some tasks than others. To understand these dynamics, we fine-tune a variety of models with three methods that apply length pressure differently, namely a fixed generation budget, a per-example length target, and a group-relative length reward. We evaluate how efficient reasoning affects CoT faithfulness (i.e., how well the CoT reflects model decisions on related inputs) and monitorability (i.e., whether the CoT reveals when input interventions alter the output). We find that it affects faithfulness and monitorability differently. Faithfulness falls in most settings, primarily because the trained models are less consistent. Monitorability is more robust, as models keep acknowledging the influence on their answer even when the CoT is much shorter.

items.title: Emerging Applications of Virtual Reality and Artificial Intelligence in Schema Therapy: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: Digital tools have become increasingly integrated into contemporary psychological practice, responding to the growing demand for accessible, scalable, and experiential mental health interventions. Within this evolving landscape, Schema Therapy represents a promising field for technological enhancement due to its emphasis on experiential techniques, mode work, and the restructuring of deeply rooted cognitive-emotional patterns. Objectives: This study aimed to map and characterize how Virtual Reality and Artificial Intelligence technologies are currently being used or proposed to support innovation in the application of Schema Therapy. Methods: A scoping review was conducted with searches performed across five major databases. Search strategies were adapted to each database, and records were screened according to inclusion/exclusion criteria. Results: Four records met eligibility criteria, revealing an emerging yet limited body of work dedicated to theoretical and experimental innovation in this area. Virtual Reality and metaverse-based interventions were proposed to create immersive, ecologically valid environments that facilitate emotional reprocessing, mode restructuring, and reductions in self-criticism, key mechanisms within ST. AI tools have demonstrated potential for large-scale identification of Early Maladaptive Schemas, enabling new forms of assessment and case conceptualization within online mental health contexts. Conclusions: No current evidence is sufficient to establish the efficacy of combining digital technologies such as Virtual Reality or Artificial Intelligence with Schema Therapy. The available literature remains limited and includes different stages of research development, from conceptual proposals and protocols to empirical studies. The identified applications primarily use these technologies as tools to support established Schema Therapy procedures rather than to modify its theoretical concepts or techniques. Although the findings indicate possible directions for technologically supported interventions, the current evidence is insufficient to establish their clinical effectiveness. Further empirical research is needed to evaluate their effects, feasibility, and clinical use within Schema Therapy.

items.title: Enhanced Visualization of Low Probability Trajectories
items.abstract: Forecast paths for hurricanes are commonly communicated through Cone of Uncertainty (COU) visualizations. An alternative visualization, animated risk trajectories (ARTs), uses dynamic ensembles of instances to convey an array of possible future tracks. Four experiments with simplified scenarios explored how surprising or misleading each form of visualization was for outcomes beyond the most likely forecast path, using participants with little direct experience (Colorado-based participants) versus more familiarity with hurricane risk and forecasts (Florida-based participants). For subsequent landfalls at locations farther from the central projected path, all participant types felt less misled when viewing ARTs rather than COUs. While Colorado-based participants reported less surprise when viewing discrepant outcomes following ARTs, Florida-based participants found deviant outcomes surprising regardless of the visualization used. items.title: Enhancing Biomedical Named Entity Recognition via Multiple Programming Languages Instruction Tuning and Ensemble Method
items.abstract: Instruction tuning has become a common paradigm for applying large language models (LLMs) to biomedical named entity recognition (BioNER). However, existing instruction-tuning approaches still face two key challenges. First, conventional natural-language instructions typically serialize BioNER annotations as flat textual outputs, providing limited structural constraints for typed entity extraction. Second, high-quality biomedical annotations are limited, and learning from a single serialized output form may restrict structural diversity and reduce model robustness. Although external biomedical knowledge can be introduced to alleviate data scarcity, it often requires costly resource construction. To address these challenges, we propose MITE, a Multiple Programming Languages Instruction Tuning and Ensemble method for BioNER. MITE reformulates BioNER as a structure-to-structure generation task by representing both instructions and entity outputs in code-formatted representations. Specifically, each training instance is transformed into multiple programming-language formats, including Python, C++, and Java, while preserving the same underlying entity semantics. These language-specific representations provide structurally diverse supervision without requiring external biomedical knowledge or additional annotations. During inference, MITE aggregates predictions from different code formats through an entity-level voting strategy, reducing language-specific prediction variance and improving robustness. Experiments on six widely used BioNER datasets demonstrate that MITE consistently outperforms representative BERT-based and LLM-based baselines and exhibits strong cross-dataset generalization. Ablation and parameter analyses further verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed components.

items.title: Enhancing Digital Library Accessibility through Artificial Intelligence for Individuals with Disabilities: A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: Digital libraries are now the main route to scholarly content, yet their content, interfaces and services still exclude many disabled users, and promotion of artificial intelligence (AI) as a remedy has outpaced evidence that it works for them. Framed by the social model of disability and the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD), this systematic literature review, reported according to PRISMA 2020, examined which AI technologies have been applied to digital library accessibility, what has been measured, and what follows for disabled users. Boolean searches of OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, the Directory of Open-Access Journals, PubMed and ERIC identified 1,056 records; after removal of 429 duplicates and two-stage screening against explicit criteria (peer-reviewed, 2016–2025, English), 26 studies were included and synthesised thematically. Speech synthesis, speech recognition, natural language processing, document AI, optical character recognition, computer vision alt text and machine learning personalisation were studied, mostly for blind and print-disabled users. Coding every claim into three registers showed that 11 studies only describe what a technology does, 13 measure system or provider-side performance, and only two report outcomes measured with disabled users, both through self-report; this absence of outcome evidence is a principal finding. Audited conformance of scholarly documents is poor; disabled people appear mainly as beneficiaries, not co-designers. The review contributes an evidence-graded, five-stage integration model that specifies actors, gates and failure handling, and recommends treating AI outputs as unverified until evaluated with disabled users. Findings rest on single-reviewer screening and published records, and the model awaits empirical testing.
